headline: A customer's class-action lawsuit accuses McDonald's of using an AI pricing tool to push up menu prices at its US restaurants.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 2: the suit was filed on 2 Oct 2026 and carried in our 6 Oct edition, and no new development was found in today's coverage.
importance_line: What changed: nothing new since the 2 Oct filing, so the case still affects diners who may pay different prices at nearby restaurants and franchise owners first, then McDonald's, and its claims are allegations that the company denies.
summary: WSB-TV, citing the Associated Press, reports that a lawsuit filed in a federal court in Illinois claims McDonald's AI-assisted pricing tool gathers sales data that competing franchisees would not normally share and raises prices, which the complaint calls "algorithmic price-fixing"; McDonald's says AI does not set menu prices and that franchisees decide. It is the suit filed on 2 Oct 2026 that our 6 Oct edition reported from Reuters, and its claims are allegations, not findings.
notes: NewsNation (the pool's source) was blocked (403), so the same story was read at WSB-TV (9 Oct 2026) and Top Class Actions (case number 1:26-cv-12149, N.D. Ill.). Older news re-dated: same suit as item 111 of our 6 Oct edition; candidate for the 14-day duplicate check.
